To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relative size of brain subdivisions varies in relation to phylogenetic constraints and to the ecology of each species.

The brain weights and brain volumes of the main subdivisions: telencepahlon, diencephalum, mesencephalon, optic tectom, cerebellum, and myelencepahlon were measured in 28 species of birds belonging 13 orders.

(i) the brain is larger in species with higher cognitive abilities; and (ii) the cerebellum is relatively larger in flying birds and the optic tectus is relatively larger in species with a high visual acuity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the allometric comparison of the brain weights and volumes in the main brain subdivisions of birds.
the comparative study of the brain in birds.
the evolution of brain structure in birds, and the relationships between brain size and the ecological and behavioral characteristics of the species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain of birds is not only highly encephalized but also highly heterencephalized.
the brain is not a simple unitary structure but is composed of a series of components, each of which has evolved at different rates and in different directions.
the size of the brain subdivisions is related to the ecological adaptations of the species and that the size of each structure can be related to its function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in birds, the relative sizes of brain structures are more closely related to ecological factors and to the importance of the sensory modalities in foraging than in mammals.
the size of the main subdivisions of the brain are related to specific ecological requirements.
the relative sizes of the telencephalic and cerebellar structures are more important in explaining the encephalization level than the size of the brainstem structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the size of the brain is a good predictor of cognitive ability, but it is not necessarily the only predictor.
the relative size of brain subdivisions in birds is related to their ecology, behavior, and sensory modalities.
the brain size of birds varies widely and that the relative sizes of different brain subdivisions are related to the lifestyle and ecology of birds.
